On we go, and sign up for the newsletter here for the full Insider experience.", "links": [{"text": "here", "url": "https://preferences.mail.deadline.com/preferences"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Turmoil At Netflix"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/GettyImages-2250243592.jpg?w=300", "alt": "", "caption": "Mario Tama/Getty Images", "credit": "Deadline · Film"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "IInternational light shines in dark: The crisis engulfing Netflix has seen the end of global content chief Bela Bajaria and film boss Dan Lim, and the introduction of former Fox and Disney TV studio topper Peter Rice. Though the company is still throwing off bundles of cash, the profits aren’t good enough for a ravenous Wall Street, and the blood of 1,000 staff has been let as Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters attempt to change the record. However, amid the ongoing troubles, the international side of the Netflix business has quietly bolstered its reputation. Though Netflix stock skidded on soft quarterly results and the lack of bonafide U.S.-made hits in 2026 has been a big problem, the streamer talked up local breakouts such as Japan’s Plastic Beauty , Denmark’s The Secret Woman , Mexico’s El Chapo and The Perfect Lie out of the Netherlands. The success of carrying the channel suite of France’s TF1 should lead to more deals of the same nature, Netflix execs added. It should be noted that none of the non-U.S. titles referenced this week could be considered global hits just yet, but there’s no doubt territory managers and regional bosses will have been heartened they’d been singled out for praise. Bajaria was popular with them, and her legacy will include the huge growth at international Netflix hubs over the past six years. As for Netflix’s new Chief Content Officer, Rice, well, there’s an international story to tell there as well. article_text:
Welcome, once again. This week, Insiders, it’s Jesse Whittock taking you through seven days in international film and TV that spans everything from major corporate layoffs to Italian festivals. On we go, and sign up for the newsletter here for the full Insider experience.

Turmoil At Netflix

IInternational light shines in dark: The crisis engulfing Netflix has seen the end of global content chief Bela Bajaria and film boss Dan Lim, and the introduction of former Fox and Disney TV studio topper Peter Rice. Though the company is still throwing off bundles of cash, the profits aren’t good enough for a ravenous Wall Street, and the blood of 1,000 staff has been let as Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters attempt to change the record. However, amid the ongoing troubles, the international side of the Netflix business has quietly bolstered its reputation. Though Netflix stock skidded on soft quarterly results and the lack of bonafide U.S.-made hits in 2026 has been a big problem, the streamer talked up local breakouts such as Japan’s Plastic Beauty , Denmark’s The Secret Woman , Mexico’s El Chapo and The Perfect Lie out of the Netherlands. The success of carrying the channel suite of France’s TF1 should lead to more deals of the same nature, Netflix execs added. It should be noted that none of the non-U.S. titles referenced this week could be considered global hits just yet, but there’s no doubt territory managers and regional bosses will have been heartened they’d been singled out for praise. Bajaria was popular with them, and her legacy will include the huge growth at international Netflix hubs over the past six years. As for Netflix’s new Chief Content Officer, Rice, well, there’s an international story to tell there as well. He was born and raised in the UK, studying at the University of Nottingham before beginning his media career at Twentieth Century Fox in 1989. Though his career has almost entirely been working for the U.S. studios, he has been known to attend the Edinburgh TV Festival and other European events, bringing hope that his strategy will continue the local-to-global model that has seen investment hit so many markets. Read Nellie Andreeva’s excellent report on his career and prospects here .

When in Rome…

From MIA to you: The latest edition of Rome’s MIA Market has been taking place this week, and I made the journey to the Italian capital for the first portion of the five-day event. Edward Berger, whose papal selection movie Conclave was set within the walls of Vatican City, opened the conference and market with a fascinating look into his filmmaking process and views on how the movie business has evolved. Berger put forwards the theory that the U.S. studios had needed the arrival of Netflix to “wake” them from a slumber, but that, given current circumstances, it might be the turn of Skydances, Disneys and NBCUniversals to inspire the streamer. MIA also heard more from Banijay Entertainment boss Marco Bassetti, speaking publicly for the second time in a week following MIPCOM in Cannes, and from Domingo Corral, the widely-respected former content boss at Spain’s Movistar Plus+, who passionately argued gatekeepers must take risks – his version of this led to greenlights for the likes of La Bola Negra and Sîrat . Elsewhere, we got a snapshot of the Italian entertainment (‘audiovisual’) market, where inward investment fell for the first time since 2018 . MIA has turned itself into an important co-production and financial market – this year’s launch of the European Investment Hub track was a sign of that – and besides the fact you can eat fabulously well in Rome (my new tip is Francesco Panella’s Antica Pesa in Trastevere), the content on offer makes it a worthy addition to an entertainment player’s schedule. More MIA here .

Watch on Deadline

The Deadline Interview: Patrick Brammall

Patrick Brammall was in reflective mood when Deadline spoke to him about his Apple TV thriller series Last Seen . The Australian actor and Harriet Dyer – his real-life wife and on-screen partner – had over the summer said goodbye to romantic sitcom Colin From Accounts and were contemplating their next steps while raising a young family in Los Angeles. Brammall opened up about what attracted him to a dramatic role in Last Seen , how he feels about leaving behind an injured dog in an Aussie comedy, and his role in The Devil Wears Prada 2 . He also gave his views on the changing shape of the Australian production scene and sent love to Brian Walsh, the late Binge commissioner who backed Colin in the first place. >>> Read The Interview

Bye Bye, BBC Three… Again

‘Fleabag’ net on the scrapheap: How many TV channels have been axed twice in 10 years? There can’t be many, but BBC Three is now one of them . The youth-skewing network is the highest-profile casualty of the BBC ‘s massive cost-cutting operation. Deadline was the first to tip the plan last month, and this week it became reality, as the axe also swung for BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra. There have been many who claim BBC Three doesn’t need a linear identity to survive given most of its target audience prefers online content, but it’s still a downer for a channel that has spawned genre-smashing shows such as Fleabag and Gavin & Stacey . In another depressing week for the UK’s public broadcaster, there were more cuts , talk of even more cuts and programs scrapped , as the BBC’s desperate bid to make the books work continues under former Google EMEA chief Matt Brittin.

The Essentials

🌶️ Hot One : J.A. Bayona, Javier Bardem and Laurent Bouzereau are teaming for Néstor , a feature doc about the life of legendary Spanish cinematographer Néstor Almendros.

🌶️ Another : Gianni Nunnari, producer on movies including the 300 franchise, is bringing Brian Selznick’s young adult novel Run Away With Me to the screen, with the author adapting his own novel.

🔥 Hot, Hot, Hot: Kari Skogland will direct Vigilant , a crime thriller based on a Skúli Sigurðsson novel and adapted for TV by Severance star Ólafur Darri Ólafsson.

🤝 New job: Carol Choi succeeded the retiring Luke Kang as President of The Walt Disney Company in Asia Pacific.

⛺ Fest latest: Walter Thompson-Hernández’s buzzy indie feature If I Go Will They Miss Me is among 10 titles screening in the International Competition at this year’s Thessaloniki Film Festival.

🏆 Interview: The story of how Olivia Colman-starrer Wicker went from an unpublished short story to a big-screen feminist romantasy, as told by the producers behind it.

⚖️ Legal: The latest from the Russell Brand trial in London. Brand denies all charges.

🌐 YouTube: Amelia Dimoldenberg’s manager, Rebecca Dowell, is spearheading an Entertainment and New Media division at her international management outfit Three Six Zero.

🇯🇵 TIFF talk: Liz Shackleton set the seen for next week’s Tokyo International Film Festival through a chat with its leaders and an interview with TIFFCOM CEO Yasushi Shiina.

😎 Madchester: Dates for the first post-Edinburgh TV Festival in Greater Manchester were announced .

🪧 Protest: Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones signed an open letter in support of their Normal People scribe Sally Rooney, whose books are banned in the UK.

👀 First look: At Minnie Driver in Paramount+ heist drama The Day .

GraphicArt, der Fotofachhändler für Profis, veranstaltet zusammen mit Sony gleich zwei Fotowalks für Freunde der Vogelfotografie. Bei so einem kostenlosen Fotowalk werden Teilnehmer von einem erfahrenen Fotoprofi durch den Veranstaltungsort, ein BirdLife-Naturzentrum mit vielen Wildvögeln, geführt. Dabei haben die Teilnehmer die Möglichkeit, Kameras und Objektive in der Praxis auszuprobieren, und sie erhalten zudem auch Tipps und Anregungen zur Vogelfotografie vom Profi.

Der eine Fotowalk findet am Donnerstag, 12. November 2026, in La Sauge am Neuenburgersee mit dem Naturfotografen Adrian Schmid statt – mehr dazu hier weiter unten. article_text:
En las instalaciones de María Abaddon (Lima, 1988) algo parece estar a punto de suceder. O, quizás, ya sucedió. En la semipenumbra del Espacio Venancio Shinki , del ICPNA , emergen figuras grotescas, blandas y coloridas, hechas con textiles y tejidos, que acaban por confundirse con formas animales, vegetales y, a toda vista, humanas. De estos volúmenes cuelgan vísceras y órganos, brotan extremidades fragmentadas, como cuerpos bajo afectación o sobrevivientes a algo que no terminamos de conocer.

Soñar con fuego , curada por Miguel A. López , reúne obras realizadas entre 2020 y 2026 y constituye la primera exposición individual de la artista en una institución de su país. La muestra continúa una investigación que en los últimos años ha hecho del cuerpo un lugar de experimentación material y conceptual. Un cuerpo que pierde sus límites, se desarma y se mezcla con otros cuerpos.

Abaddon llama a su estética «gore soft». En la expresión conviven aquello que asociamos con la violencia —la carne abierta, la herida, el desmembramiento— y figuras construidas con materiales que aluden al cuidado y la intimidad, como la lana, el fieltro, el crochet y el bordado. Cuerpos blandos es otra forma de describirlos. Cuerpos en desintegración, donde las suturas y los remiendos quedan expuestos como cicatrices.

Una cabeza sin individuo, un torso sin identidad, una masa de órganos que podría pertenecer a varios entes al mismo tiempo. La artista arma conjuntos por acumulación hasta alcanzar, en ocasiones, escalas monumentales. El proceso es laborioso y consume tiempo, por lo que cuenta con la colaboración de otras personas para su producción.

Abaddon ha explicado que evita deliberadamente introducir marcas de raza, género o identidad en sus personajes. Le interesa que sus bordes no estén definidos y que puedan mezclarse como ocurre en sociedades y comunidades. Pero esas marcas reaparecen inevitablemente en las obras, aunque sea a través de metáforas de la condición humana, desde el ser vulnerable y parte de una masa, hasta perder la forma y volver a erguirse.

Es una preocupación que viene de antes. En Suave por dentro , exposición presentada a comienzos de 2026 en el Ministerio de Cultura peruano, la artista presentó esculturas textiles, como Los centauros comen carne cruda (2022) y Te mira de vuelta (2025), que conciben el cuerpo como materia en constante transformación. En Soñar con fuego , sin embargo, esa transformación se vuelve más expansiva. Las criaturas ya no parecen solamente cuerpos heridos: podrían ser los habitantes de un mundo posterior al desastre.

Tienen algo de ciencia ficción, pero también de fantasía fúngica, de organismo mutante, de resto arqueológico. La influencia de películas como Akira y Tetsuo: The Iron Man, y producciones de serie B como Tokyo Gore Police , ayuda a entender ese imaginario donde el cuerpo pierde autonomía y las fronteras entre lo humano y lo monstruoso se difuminan.

Pero Abaddon vuelve esos imaginarios blandos, domésticos y táctiles. Mientras el cyberpunk suele imaginar máquinas que invaden o modifican el cuerpo, la artista construye máquinas precarias que conviven con él. Sus circuitos, sensores y arduinos no buscan producir una ilusión tecnológica sofisticada. Al contrario, exhiben su funcionamiento.

En la exposición, algunas piezas responden a la presencia del público mediante sensores de distancia. Se mueven apenas, como si percibieran que alguien se aproxima. No hay aquí inteligencia artificial ni reconocimiento complejo, sino una programación sencilla y una reacción mecánica. La artista ha insistido en esa diferencia, en su interés por generar una forma rudimentaria de sensibilidad.

El título de la muestra es menos apocalíptico de lo que parece. Soñar con fuego no habla únicamente de un mundo que se quema. Habla también de lo que puede imaginarse después. En Paisaje de la destrucción (2024), una obra incluida en la XXXII Subasta de Arte Textil del MALI, las formas rojas podrían sugerir un incendio en expansión, pero la paleta luminosa y la suavidad del fieltro alteran esa lectura. La escena resulta, a la vez, inquietante y amable.

Esa ambivalencia se refleja en toda la exposición. El fuego destruye, pero también transforma. El cuerpo se desintegra y, sin embargo, sus fragmentos pueden reorganizarse. Una identidad puede desaparecer, y de esa pérdida puede surgir otra forma de existencia. Coser y tejer significa también que una trama puede deshacerse y volver a hacerse. Frente a una cultura tecnológica cada vez más orientada hacia la velocidad, la eficiencia y la descorporización, Abaddon insiste en procesos lentos y manuales. Su tecnología funciona casi como un organismo rudimentario que se equivoca, tiembla y responde tarde.

¿Llegará ese punto en la historia cuando ya no podamos distinguir con claridad entre humano, animal, planta, máquina y paisaje? ¿Qué tipo de sensibilidad puede nacer de esa mezcla? En la obra de Abaddon, la ternura y el horror funcionan como dos posibilidades de una misma materia. Sus criaturas no ofrecen una moraleja sobre la violencia o el colapso. Están ahí, blandas y perturbadoras, como si hubieran aprendido a vivir en un mundo que todavía no sabemos nombrar.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 同步维度：今年纽约电影节（NYFF）的三部由巴勒斯坦人制作或以巴勒斯坦人为主题的电影，撬开了几个视窗，让我们不得不去理解加沙的地平线与我们自身的命运紧密相连
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我们的时间并不遵循过去、现在和未来的轴线，”巴勒斯坦政治犯兼小说家瓦利德·达卡（Walid Daqqa）在即将成为无期徒刑的将近20年后写道。达卡尖锐地将监狱中无限延展却从不向前推进的“平行时间”与外界的历时性时间进行了对比；然而他十分清楚，对于巴勒斯坦人来说，监狱并没有在牢门处结束。后来，在反思他年幼的女儿对他的处境的直觉理解时，达卡将监狱定义为一个“没有门的地方”。这句话精辟地总结了巴勒斯坦人在以色列占领下的生存状态，尤其是（但不仅限于）那些今天在加沙被围困的废墟中维系生命的人们。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "卡马尔·阿尔贾法里（Kamal Aljafari）的《与哈桑在加沙》（With Hasan in Gaza）入选了第63届纽约电影节（NYFF63）的“视野”（Currents）单元，它逆着历时性时间，将我们带回2001年那个加沙仍然伫立、且巴勒斯坦电影人尚能进入的时期——那是在第二次大起义期间、以色列封锁之前。阿尔贾法里这部安静而萦绕心头的电影取材于他当时拍摄的 MiniDV 磁带——当时他还没有拍摄他的第一部短片、即2003年的《访问伊拉克》（Visit Iraq ）——这些磁带最近被重新发现。它记录了这位电影人寻找一位加沙朋友的过程，两人在青少年时期曾共用一间牢房。这部《与哈桑》完全由这些“寻获的”素材组成，在当下通过字幕进行极简的画幅框定，字幕传达着他的监狱回忆，配乐则将稀疏、诡异的合成器音乐与精心挑选的巴勒斯坦及阿拉伯歌曲交织在一起，这些歌曲的歌词在加沙遭受毁灭的背景下赋予了这些影像新的含义。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《与哈桑》的大部分悲剧力量在于我们与加沙昔日充满活力、微笑着的孩子们嬉戏、新鲜蔬菜琳琅满目的街道和市集进行的不合时宜的相遇。但以色列占领带来的废墟、征服和贫困也同样存在于此；《与哈桑》无法逃离达卡式的监狱，这既是它的主题，也是我们审视加沙的透镜。阿尔贾法里最初呈现的画面是他为进入加沙而穿过的以色列军事基础设施；镜头拉近了一个无人看守的哨卡，就好像他攫取了观察者的角色，仅仅是为了驱散监视的目光。从这里开始，阿尔贾法里为我们呈现了加沙两日两夜的亲密记录，他的朋友兼向导哈桑·埃尔布布（Hasan Elboubou）和他自己成为了我们的同行者。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在电影中，加沙很少能获得如此细致、温柔的观察——这种观察试图从邻居和朋友而非记者或救援人员的角度去了解这个地方。（重要的例外包括阿卜杜勒·萨拉姆·谢哈达〔Abdel Salam Shehada〕充满眷恋的2008年纪录片《致我的父亲》〔To My Father〕，以及米歇尔·克莱菲〔Michel Khleifi〕奇妙的1995年剧情片《三颗珠宝的故事》〔Tale of the Three Jewels〕，这是第一部完全在加沙拍摄的故事片。）《与哈桑》令人心酸，不仅因为它描绘了加沙被消灭之前的面貌，还因为它以一种充满爱意的好奇心探索了那里的生活世界，这与拯救加沙或代其发言毫无关系。他的镜头具有触觉且充满活力；我们感觉自己仿佛正用手抚过狭窄小巷的墙壁，在咖啡馆里闲坐着看男人们打牌，或者坐在汽车的副驾驶座上凝视着窗外。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿尔贾法里遇到的每个人都指挥他把镜头指向这或指向那，无论是大喊“拍我！”的孩子们，还是恳求他记录以色列暴力的成年人。仅就这一点而言，《与哈桑》就像许多以第二次大起义为背景的纪录片一样，充斥着挥之不去的哨卡、废墟和呼喊的过路人的影像——但阿尔贾法里默默地让他的目光漫游。哈桑有时也拿着相机，拍摄阿尔贾法里与不同个人的对话：一位在以色列监狱度过了8年时间的父亲，他说自己在海滩上陪伴孩子，以弥补失去的时光；一位站在被以色列军队摧毁的房屋废墟上的农民，他担心被拍摄，因为他有一张“电子工卡”。他的一位邻居安慰他说不会有人看到这部电影，却无意中让他成为了加沙具有预言意义的代名词：“我们正在准备一部将在多年后上映的纪录片。你在里面都不会被认出来。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "加沙人民的幽灵般痕迹也成为了塞皮黛·法尔西（Sepideh Farsi）入选第63届纽约电影节焦点单元的《把灵魂放在手上行走》（Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk ）的意外主题。这是一部关于巴勒斯坦摄影记者兼诗人法特玛·哈苏纳（Fatma Hassouna）的纪录片，她于今年早些时候遇害，年仅25岁。这位流亡的伊朗电影人被阻无法进入加沙，在开罗通过一位流离失所的巴勒斯坦人得知哈苏纳后，与她结下了友谊，并在她身上找到了一个同样“受制于墙壁与战争”的灵魂伴侣。影片的结构是两位女性在2024年4月至2025年4月期间视频通话的纪年日记，其间被信号中断和轰炸打断，并穿插着新闻片段。我们在法尔西拍摄的支架手机屏幕上看到了哈苏纳；她毫无防备的微笑、对加沙的热爱以及与这位电影人交流时的明显喜悦，与她向我们展示的毁灭场景构成了令人心碎的对照。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“如果我必须死，我希望死得轰轰烈烈，”哈苏娜写道，她遥相呼应了诗人兼教授里法特·阿莱里（Refaat Alareer）如今广为人知的名言（由巴图尔·阿布·阿克林［Batool Abu Akleen］译出），随后她迎来了与后者相同的命运。法尔西在《Put Your Soul》中令人钦佩地放大了哈苏娜的生命、创造力与坚定的希望，片中数段影像将哈苏娜的照片与她的诗歌、歌曲及评论生动地结合在一起。这位电影人还极具说服力地克制了任何将拍摄对象视为受害者或纯真者的冲动；相反，这位常驻巴黎与雅典的世俗伊朗异见人士，经常让这位年龄与她女儿相仿的女子之间产生种种分歧——后者从未有机会离开加沙，并坚信上帝对一切都有安排，包括加沙的苦难（法尔西对此公开且礼貌地表示异议）。然而，这段关系发展的时间却悲剧般地短暂。在他们的最后一次对话中，法尔西告知哈苏娜该片已入选戛纳；两人讨论了让哈苏娜飞去戛纳的事，而哈苏娜坚称自己一定会回到她的家乡加沙。字幕告诉我们，就在那天晚上，哈苏娜在公寓中遭以色列空袭身亡，多位家人亦同日遇难，她也加入了自2023年10月以来遇难的200多名巴勒斯坦记者的行列。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴斯马·阿尔-谢里夫（Basma al-Sharif）时长21分钟的实验短片《早会》（Morning Circle）入选了纽约电影节的“现当代浪潮”单元，它发生的地方并非加沙，而是在柏林——这里回荡着过去及正在进行的种族灭绝的回响。（这位导演在加沙、美国和法国长大，目前定居德国。）她的影片讲述了作为一名移民，在一个将非人化的同化标准作为其好客代价的国家里如何为人父母，或者说，讲述了拒绝这种代价所能寻得的尊严。故事设定在一个早晨，其松散的叙事围绕着赫尔·亚伯拉罕扬（帕诺斯·阿普拉哈米安饰）与一位未出镜的德国官僚之间紧张的对话展开，后者显然在亚伯拉罕扬的公寓内盘问他关于其“对我们这里生活方式的执念”。亚伯拉罕扬证实，除其他外，他会说阿拉伯语但并非穆斯林；其亚美尼亚-阿拉伯身份召唤出了一系列人口管理系统所无法理解的流离失所与情感羁绊。但阿尔-谢里夫并不关心去揭露官僚的问题（“你想回去吗？”）如何建立在不可能二分法的基础上；亚伯拉罕扬对此予以回绝，冷静地抽着烟，然后走开去唤醒他幼小的儿子阿德南（穆罕默德·阿里饰）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "德国人的提问在全片大部分时间里回荡，伴随着亚伯拉罕扬和阿德南走进阿德南的音乐幼儿园（musikkindergarten）。然而，声音上的呼应与远方故土的吉光片羽也同样如此。亚伯拉罕扬给儿子剪指甲，同时我们听到他们正在收听来自加沙的阿拉伯语新闻；反打镜头展示了电视屏幕，但映入眼帘的并非死亡与毁灭的景象，而是地中海海岸。点缀在影片沉思基调中的是开罗莫里斯·卢卡（Maurice Louca）的一首地下电子赞歌《向鹦鹉致敬》（“Salute the Parrot”），其古怪的副歌与沙比（shaabi）节奏在家庭公寓的寂静中泛起涟漪，随后在学校影片最后的舞蹈段落中爆发。这是一个充满活力的结局，镜头随幼儿园的孩子们一起旋转舞蹈，透过迷幻的色彩进行过滤，并叠加了加沙巴勒斯坦人在（一月的停火期间）重返家园的画面。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部影片可能会让一些人觉得轻浮（哦，德国，总是站在错误的一边）或是荒诞（醒醒吧，向鹦鹉致敬？），但作为一名身处侨民身份的巴勒斯坦-黎巴嫩父亲，我发现它深深地打动了我。阿尔-谢里夫采用的反复手法——回音、叠印、突发——在此唤起了爱德华·萨义德（Edward Said）对流亡者对位视角的礼赞，即他们“对同时代维度的感知”。与此同时，亚伯拉罕扬照顾阿德南的场景提醒我们，在历经了一场夺去、伤害或孤老了无数成千上万儿童生命的种族灭绝之中，建立家庭意味着什么（对于这场浩劫，诸如“妇女和儿童”的伤亡统计数字无论出于何种善意，都是对巴勒斯坦男性温柔之情的冒犯）。这里呈现的是一幅万花筒般的景象，展现了无论我们住在哪里，加沙在我们内心产生共鸣意味着什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我想起哈苏娜拍摄的一张照片，画面中是一堵被炸开的混凝土墙；阳光从洞口倾泻而入，透过它，我们看到两辆车停在海天一线的地平线之下。这是一幅废墟的影像，还是充满可能的影像？如果监狱是一个没有门的场所，那么这三部风格迥异的电影，正强行撬开通往平行时空的狭缝，我们必须从中去理解加沙的地平线，因为它与我们自身的命运紧密相连。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Our time does not proceed on the axis of past and present and future,” wrote the Palestinian political prisoner and novelist Walid Daqqa, nearly 20 years into what would become a life sentence. Daqqa poignantly contrasted the “parallel time” of prison, stretching out indefinitely though never moving forward, with the chronological time outside; yet he understood well that for Palestinians, prison does not end at the cell doors. Later, reflecting on his young daughter’s intuitive understanding of his condition, Daqqa would define prison as a “place without a door.” It’s a phrase that distills much about Palestinian existence under Israeli occupation, particularly, though not only, for those holding onto life in the besieged rubble of Gaza today."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Kamal Aljafari’s With Hasan in Gaza , screening in the Currents section of NYFF63, returns us, bucking chronological time, to a Gaza still standing and accessible to the Palestinian filmmaker in 2001—during the Second Intifada but prior to Israel’s blockade. Aljafari’s quiet and haunting film is made from MiniDV tapes he shot back then—before he had made his first short, 2003’s Visit Iraq —and recently rediscovered. It documents the filmmaker’s search for a friend from Gaza with whom he shared a prison cell as a teenager. Composed entirely of this “found” footage, With Hasan is minimally framed, in the present, by captions relaying his prison memories and a soundtrack that alternates sparse, eerie synth work with brilliantly selected Palestinian and Arab songs, whose lyrics recast the images in light of Gaza’s destruction."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Much of With Hasan ’s pathos lies in our anachronistic encounter with Gaza’s once-vibrant streets and souks, where smiling children play and fresh vegetables abound. But the rubble, subjugation, and poverty wrought by Israeli occupation are here too; With Hasan cannot escape from Daqqa’s prison, which is both its subject and the prism through which we see Gaza. Aljafari’s first images are of the Israeli military infrastructure through which he passes to enter Gaza; zooming in on an unattended checkpoint, it is as if he seizes the role of the watcher only to exorcise the surveillant gaze. From here on, Aljafari gives us an intimate record of two days and two nights in Gaza, with his friend and guide Hasan Elboubou and himself serving as our companions."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Rarely in cinema is Gaza granted the care of close, tender observation that seeks to know the place from the perspective of a neighbor and friend rather than a journalist or emergency worker. (Important exceptions include Abdel Salam Shehada’s wistful 2008 documentary To My Father and Michel Khleifi’s wondrous 1995 drama Tale of the Three Jewels , the first narrative feature shot entirely in Gaza.) With Hasan is poignant not only because it depicts Gaza before its annihilation, but because Aljafari explores its lifeworlds with a loving curiosity that has nothing to do with saving it or speaking on its behalf. His camera is tactile and active; we feel we are running our hands along the walls of narrow alleyways, idling in a café watching men play cards, or sitting in the passenger seat of a car and gazing out its window."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Everyone Aljafari encounters commands him to point the camera here or there, whether it is children shouting “film me!” or adults imploring him to document Israeli violence. In this respect alone, With Hasan is like many a documentary set during the Second Intifada, with their inescapable imagery of checkpoints, rubble, and shouting passersby—but Aljafari quietly lets his gaze wander. Hasan also holds the camera at times, showing Aljafari in conversation with various individuals: a father who spent eight years in Israeli prisons and says he’s at the beach making up for lost time with his children; a farmer standing atop the debris of homes destroyed by the Israeli army, who worries about being filmed because he has an “electronic worker card.” A neighbor of his reassures him that no one will see the film, and unwittingly makes him a prophetic synecdoche for Gaza: “We’re preparing a documentary that will be shown many years from now. You wouldn’t be recognizable in it.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The ghostly traces of Gaza’s people also become the unanticipated subject of Sepideh Farsi’s NYFF63 Spotlight selection Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk , a documentary about Palestinian photojournalist and poet Fatma Hassouna, who was killed earlier this year at the age of 25. Blocked from entering Gaza, the exiled Iranian filmmaker struck up a friendship with Hassouna after hearing of her through a displaced Palestinian in Cairo, and finding in her a kindred spirit also “conditioned by walls and wars.” The film is structured as a chronological diary of the two women’s video calls between April 2024 and April 2025, interrupted by connectivity failures and bombings, and interspersed with news clips. We see Hassouna on the screen of a mounted cell phone, filmed by Farsi; her unguarded smile, love of Gaza, and evident joy in connecting with the filmmaker are devastating counterpoints to the scenes of destruction she shows us."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“If I must die, I want a resonant death,” Hassouna wrote, before she met the same fate as poet and professor Refaat Alareer, whose now-famous words (as translated by Batool Abu Akleen) she echoes. Farsi has admirably amplified her life, creativity, and steadfast hope in Put Your Soul , which features several sequences that vividly pair Hassouna’s photographs with her poems, songs, and commentary. The filmmaker also compellingly resists any urge to speak with her subject as a victim or naïf; instead, the secular, Paris- and Athens-based Iranian dissident frequently allows differences to emerge between herself and a woman her daughter’s age, who never had a chance to leave Gaza and who believes that God has a reason for everything, including Gaza’s suffering (Farsi openly, politely, disagrees). But there is tragically little time for this relationship to develop. In their final conversation, Farsi informs Hassouna that the film has been accepted to Cannes; the two discuss flying out Hassouna, who insists she will return to Gaza, her home. That night, captions inform us, Hassouna was killed in her apartment by an Israeli air strike, together with several family members, joining more than 200 Palestinian journalists killed since October 2023."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Basma al-Sharif’s 21-minute experimental short Morning Circle , featured in the NYFF’s Currents program, takes place not in Gaza but amid the reverberations of genocides past and ongoing, in Berlin. (The director was raised in Gaza, the U.S., and France, and now lives in Germany.) article_text:
“Our time does not proceed on the axis of past and present and future,” wrote the Palestinian political prisoner and novelist Walid Daqqa, nearly 20 years into what would become a life sentence. Daqqa poignantly contrasted the “parallel time” of prison, stretching out indefinitely though never moving forward, with the chronological time outside; yet he understood well that for Palestinians, prison does not end at the cell doors. Later, reflecting on his young daughter’s intuitive understanding of his condition, Daqqa would define prison as a “place without a door.” It’s a phrase that distills much about Palestinian existence under Israeli occupation, particularly, though not only, for those holding onto life in the besieged rubble of Gaza today.

Kamal Aljafari’s With Hasan in Gaza , screening in the Currents section of NYFF63, returns us, bucking chronological time, to a Gaza still standing and accessible to the Palestinian filmmaker in 2001—during the Second Intifada but prior to Israel’s blockade. Aljafari’s quiet and haunting film is made from MiniDV tapes he shot back then—before he had made his first short, 2003’s Visit Iraq —and recently rediscovered. It documents the filmmaker’s search for a friend from Gaza with whom he shared a prison cell as a teenager. Composed entirely of this “found” footage, With Hasan is minimally framed, in the present, by captions relaying his prison memories and a soundtrack that alternates sparse, eerie synth work with brilliantly selected Palestinian and Arab songs, whose lyrics recast the images in light of Gaza’s destruction.

Much of With Hasan ’s pathos lies in our anachronistic encounter with Gaza’s once-vibrant streets and souks, where smiling children play and fresh vegetables abound. But the rubble, subjugation, and poverty wrought by Israeli occupation are here too; With Hasan cannot escape from Daqqa’s prison, which is both its subject and the prism through which we see Gaza. Aljafari’s first images are of the Israeli military infrastructure through which he passes to enter Gaza; zooming in on an unattended checkpoint, it is as if he seizes the role of the watcher only to exorcise the surveillant gaze. From here on, Aljafari gives us an intimate record of two days and two nights in Gaza, with his friend and guide Hasan Elboubou and himself serving as our companions.

Rarely in cinema is Gaza granted the care of close, tender observation that seeks to know the place from the perspective of a neighbor and friend rather than a journalist or emergency worker. (Important exceptions include Abdel Salam Shehada’s wistful 2008 documentary To My Father and Michel Khleifi’s wondrous 1995 drama Tale of the Three Jewels , the first narrative feature shot entirely in Gaza.) With Hasan is poignant not only because it depicts Gaza before its annihilation, but because Aljafari explores its lifeworlds with a loving curiosity that has nothing to do with saving it or speaking on its behalf. His camera is tactile and active; we feel we are running our hands along the walls of narrow alleyways, idling in a café watching men play cards, or sitting in the passenger seat of a car and gazing out its window.

Everyone Aljafari encounters commands him to point the camera here or there, whether it is children shouting “film me!” or adults imploring him to document Israeli violence. In this respect alone, With Hasan is like many a documentary set during the Second Intifada, with their inescapable imagery of checkpoints, rubble, and shouting passersby—but Aljafari quietly lets his gaze wander. Hasan also holds the camera at times, showing Aljafari in conversation with various individuals: a father who spent eight years in Israeli prisons and says he’s at the beach making up for lost time with his children; a farmer standing atop the debris of homes destroyed by the Israeli army, who worries about being filmed because he has an “electronic worker card.” A neighbor of his reassures him that no one will see the film, and unwittingly makes him a prophetic synecdoche for Gaza: “We’re preparing a documentary that will be shown many years from now. You wouldn’t be recognizable in it.”

The ghostly traces of Gaza’s people also become the unanticipated subject of Sepideh Farsi’s NYFF63 Spotlight selection Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk , a documentary about Palestinian photojournalist and poet Fatma Hassouna, who was killed earlier this year at the age of 25. Blocked from entering Gaza, the exiled Iranian filmmaker struck up a friendship with Hassouna after hearing of her through a displaced Palestinian in Cairo, and finding in her a kindred spirit also “conditioned by walls and wars.” The film is structured as a chronological diary of the two women’s video calls between April 2024 and April 2025, interrupted by connectivity failures and bombings, and interspersed with news clips. We see Hassouna on the screen of a mounted cell phone, filmed by Farsi; her unguarded smile, love of Gaza, and evident joy in connecting with the filmmaker are devastating counterpoints to the scenes of destruction she shows us.

“If I must die, I want a resonant death,” Hassouna wrote, before she met the same fate as poet and professor Refaat Alareer, whose now-famous words (as translated by Batool Abu Akleen) she echoes. Farsi has admirably amplified her life, creativity, and steadfast hope in Put Your Soul , which features several sequences that vividly pair Hassouna’s photographs with her poems, songs, and commentary. The filmmaker also compellingly resists any urge to speak with her subject as a victim or naïf; instead, the secular, Paris- and Athens-based Iranian dissident frequently allows differences to emerge between herself and a woman her daughter’s age, who never had a chance to leave Gaza and who believes that God has a reason for everything, including Gaza’s suffering (Farsi openly, politely, disagrees). But there is tragically little time for this relationship to develop. In their final conversation, Farsi informs Hassouna that the film has been accepted to Cannes; the two discuss flying out Hassouna, who insists she will return to Gaza, her home. That night, captions inform us, Hassouna was killed in her apartment by an Israeli air strike, together with several family members, joining more than 200 Palestinian journalists killed since October 2023.

Basma al-Sharif’s 21-minute experimental short Morning Circle , featured in the NYFF’s Currents program, takes place not in Gaza but amid the reverberations of genocides past and ongoing, in Berlin. (The director was raised in Gaza, the U.S., and France, and now lives in Germany.) Her film is about parenting as an immigrant in a country that sets a dehumanizing standard of assimilation as the cost of its hospitality—or rather, about the dignity to be found in refusing that price. Set during a single morning, its loose narrative is structured around a tense exchange between Herr Abrahamyan (Panos Aprahamian) and an off-screen German bureaucrat who interrogates him, apparently within his own apartment, about his “attachment to our way of life here.” Abrahamyan attests, among other things, that he speaks Arabic but is not Muslim; his Armenian-Arab identity summons a plurality of displacements and attachments opaque to systems of population management. But al-Sharif is not concerned with exposing how the bureaucrat’s questions (“Would you like to go back?”) rest on impossible binaries; Abrahamyan balks at them, coolly smokes his cigarette, and walks away to wake his young son Adnan (Mohammad Ali).

The German’s questions echo across much of the film, trailing Abrahamyan and Adnan as they enter Adnan’s musikkindergarten . But so too do sonic rejoinders and glimpses of distant homelands. Abrahamyan clips his son’s fingernails as we hear them listening to Arabic-language news from Gaza; a countershot shows the TV screen, but rather than images of death and destruction, we see the Mediterranean coast. Punctuating the pensive tone of the film is an electronic underground anthem by Cairo’s Maurice Louca, “Salute the Parrot,” whose zany chorus and shaabi beats bubble up in the quiet of the family apartment before erupting in the film’s final dance sequence at the school. It’s an exuberant ending, the camera whirling with the kindergarten children as they dance, filtered through psychedelic colors and overlayed with images of Gaza’s Palestinians returning to their homes (during January’s ceasefire).

The film may strike some as flippant ( oh Germany, always on the wrong side ) or absurdist ( wake up and salute the parrot? ), but, as a diasporic Palestinian-Lebanese father, I found it deeply moving. The recurrent techniques employed by al-Sharif—echoes, superimpositions, irruptions—here evoke Edward Said’s celebration of the exile’s contrapuntal vision, their “awareness of simultaneous dimensions.” Scenes of Abrahamyan caring for Adnan, meanwhile, remind us of what it is to build family amid a genocide that has killed, injured, or orphaned countless thousands upon thousands of children (and for which casualty counts of “women and children,” however well-intended, are an affront to the tenderness of Palestinian men). Here is one kaleidoscopic view of what it means for Gaza to resonate within us, wherever we live.

I think of a photo by Hassouna, of a concrete wall blasted open; sunlight streams in from the hole, and through it, we see two cars parked under a horizon of sea and sky. Is it an image of ruination or possibility? If prison is a place without a door, these three films, distinct as they are, pry open apertures into a parallel time and space, from which we must make sense of Gaza’s horizon as intimately tied to our own.

article_text:
The artist’s installation at Secession is undoubtedly spectacular, but does it move beyond that?

Mire Lee’s largescale installation transforms the Secession’s main gallery into an abattoir. Red liquid (a viscous mixture of water, iron oxide, methylcellulose and sawdust, among other ingredients) drains down a stained sheet-metal slope that makes up one wall and puddles under a floor constructed of metal grids. At its heart rests the bleached white barrel of a concrete-mixer truck, sliced open to reveal its spiralling, red-splattered ribs as it revolves, like the bloated corpse of an eviscerated whale in perpetual agony. Connected by cables and tubes, each part of the installation seems to be connected as part of a closedsystem ouroboroslike whole, reconstituting the gallery as an industrial machine, the industrial machine as an organic form and the whole building as an ecosystem, each stage chewing through or overwriting the one that precedes it. And each of which, be it translation or metaphor, might be one way of describing what the Secession itself, or any exhibition space for that matter, is.

If the cement mixer is carved open, so is the Secession, with natural light now penetrating its stripped-back roof. While a row of whitewashed promotional banners for past exhibitions has been skied across the wall opposite the metal slope, and onto which words such as GOLD, MUTTERNAME (mother’s name) and GALLENSAFT (bile) have been added in brass leaf, alongside Korean characters graffitied in black paint. That you can still make out some of the original promotional texts in reverse gives the panels the feeling of a multilingual, multicultural palimpsest: a mirror to the layered metaphors offered by the sculpture as a whole. But it would be a stretch to say that the work, while undoubtedly spectacular, ever moves much beyond that: it’s all brutal, poetic form rather than content or a message in and of itself. For some of those last, you need to traipse (about ten minutes) over to the Korean Cultural Center, where three of Lee’s earlier videoworks are on show in a parallel show titled Women I loved . Each of which presents the female body in a different context: Sleeping Mom (2020) features the artist’s mother, on loop, doing what it says in the title; Faces (2016), which focuses on the faces of Japanese women riding the subway shortly before they are about to be groped (excerpted from pornography); and Veronica Moser (2022), which presents an edited interview with the eponymous Austrian pornstar and scatologist, who describes how from being bored as a secretary she moved into nude modelling, to pornography and, eventually, to shit-eating. In these works, the subjects are an embodied form of all that is abstracted in the installation at the Secession. In each video the question of whether or not the subject’s actions come of their own volition is raised in a different manner. Questions of agency and ownership are in play, as well as what it is that makes us something more than a system of chemistry, physics and biology, all of which gives these works a feeling of greater depth and sophistication than the big brash sculpture at the Secession.

Mire Lee: The Heart of My Machine is Golden Lead was at Secession, Vienna, 26 June – 26 August

article_text:
Obituary

Ursula von Rydingsvard, Who Sculpted Monuments of Cedar, Dies at 84

"She was like the sun. She was this force that pulled people in and kept them orbiting around her," said her studio manager.

Ursula von Rydingsvard, a sculptor whose monumental objects were partly inspired by her childhood in post-World War II refugee camps, died in her Manhattan home this morning, October 27, at 84. The artist's studio manager, Courtney Childress, attributed Von Rydingsvard's death to Alzheimer's disease, according to the New York Times .

During her over five-decade career, Von Rydingsvard chipped away at enormous cedar beams to create a menagerie of massive sculptures, from an assembly of cones to a 17-foot-tall tornado-shaped behemoth made from 15,000 pounds of wood. The abstract sculptor worked with an array of other materials , including bronze, textiles, and animal intestines.

"She was like the sun. She was this force that pulled people in and kept them orbiting around her," Childress told Hyperallergic in a phone interview. "She moved through the studio like her hair was on fire, and could never slow down."

Born in 1942 in Deensen, Germany, in the midst of World War II, to a Polish mother and a Ukrainian father, Von Rydingsvard took significant inspiration from her childhood experiences. When the war ended in 1945, her family of nine navigated eight Nazi slave-labor and postwar refugee camps before taking a military ship to the United States in 1950, as she relayed in an interview with Art 21 .

While she resisted autobiographical readings of her oeuvre, her observations of the wooden barracks in camps and pre-industrial wooden Polish homes informed her preferred medium of cedar, she continued in the interview. Other memories, from the feeling of a linen nightgown to the sun warming her body, created a reservoir of inspiration for her works.

She went on to obtain a Bachelor of Arts and a Master of Arts from the University of Miami in 1965, and earned a Master of Fine Arts in studio art from Columbia University in 1975.

Recipient of a spate of honors, including the Guggenheim Fellowship, the Joan Mitchell Fellowship, and grants from the National Endowment for the Arts, Von Rydingsvard gained widespread recognition for translating visual cues of human anatomy, the environment, and household vessels into large-scale pieces, departing from the aloof nature of 1970s minimalism. She was the subject of solo exhibitions at the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the National Museum in Krakow, and the Yorkshire Sculpture Park in the United Kingdom, and her work is in the permanent collections of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Museum of Modern Art, and the Whitney Museum of American Art in Manhattan.

article_text:
Prime Video presentó el adelanto de la nueva temporada de El Señor de los Anillos: Los Anillos de Poder , que llegará en noviembre con Sauron cada vez más cerca de forjar el Anillo Único.

La guerra por el destino de la Tierra Media está a punto de alcanzar un nuevo nivel. Prime Video presentó el tráiler oficial de la tercera temporada de El Señor de los Anillos: Los Anillos de Poder , la serie de fantasía que regresa con una historia marcada por el avance de Sauron, la amenaza de sus ejércitos y la creación del Anillo Único para gobernarlos a todos.

«Todo ha conducido a esto», afirma Galadriel en el adelanto, que anticipa una nueva etapa en la lucha contra el Señor Oscuro. Los elfos, los enanos y los hombres deberán encontrar la manera de unir sus fuerzas para frenar el avance de las fuerzas del mal, mientras Sauron se prepara para consolidar su dominio sobre la Tierra Media.

¿De qué trata la tercera temporada de Los Anillos de Poder?

La nueva entrega transcurre cinco años después de la caída de Eregion. Durante ese período, los ejércitos de Sauron avanzaron por distintos territorios, conquistando tierras y acercándose a una victoria que parece cada vez más posible. Sin embargo, todavía quedan enclaves que resisten el avance del Señor Oscuro, entre ellos Khazad-dûm y los reinos élficos de Lindon y Rivendel.

Mientras sus enemigos intentan reorganizarse, Sauron trabaja desde la torre de Barad-dûr, en Mordor, para alcanzar su objetivo definitivo: forjar el Anillo Único y obtener un poder capaz de someter a todos los pueblos de la Tierra Media.

El tráiler también anticipa conflictos en distintos frentes. Los elfos lucharán por mantener sus posiciones, los vínculos familiares de los enanos de Khazad-dûm atravesarán momentos críticos y Númenor quedará al borde de una guerra civil. En las tierras orientales de Rhûn, Gandalf también tendrá un papel importante en la batalla contra la oscuridad que amenaza con extenderse por el mundo.

Carrie tendrá segunda temporada en Prime Video: Mike Flanagan prepara más terror

Con la guerra en marcha y el poder de Sauron en ascenso, los pueblos libres deberán dejar de lado sus diferencias para evitar que el Señor Oscuro consiga imponer su voluntad sobre toda forma de vida.

¿Cuándo se estrena la tercera temporada de Los Anillos de Poder?

La tercera temporada de El Señor de los Anillos: Los Anillos de Poder llegará a Prime Video el 11 de noviembre de 2026 , con un estreno dividido en tres tandas de episodios.

Los primeros cuatro capítulos estarán disponibles ese día. El 18 de noviembre se estrenarán los episodios cinco y seis, mientras que los dos capítulos finales llegarán el 25 de noviembre.

La serie, desarrollada por J. D. Payne y Patrick McKay, está ambientada miles de años antes de los acontecimientos de El Hobbit y El Señor de los Anillos . A través de nuevas historias y personajes conocidos del universo creado por J. R. R. Tolkien, la producción explora los acontecimientos de la Segunda Edad, cuando surgieron grandes poderes y comenzó a tomar forma una de las amenazas más importantes de la historia de la Tierra Media.

Con Sauron decidido a completar su obra y el Anillo Único cada vez más cerca, la tercera temporada promete profundizar en una de las etapas más decisivas de este universo fantástico.

URCHIN アーチン

劇場公開日： 2026年10月23日

映画館を探す

予告編を見る

映画チケットを U-NEXTでお得にゲット PR

解説・あらすじ

「逆転のトライアングル」「ベイビーガール」で世界的に注目を浴びたイギリス出身の俳優ハリス・ディキンソンの長編映画監督デビュー作。路上生活者や依存者の支援団体をサポートしてきた経験に着想を得て、ディキンソン監督が自ら脚本も執筆。生活力もモラルもない路上生活者の青年が、変わることを切望しながらも転落していく姿をユーモアを交えて描き、社会の隙間に落ちた人々と、そこから抜け出せない社会システムを映し出す。 ロンドンの路上で暮らすマイクは、通行人に小銭を要求したり、炊き出しの列に並んだりと忙しい日々を過ごしている。そんなある日、彼は親切にしてくれた男性から衝動的に金品を奪ってしまい、逮捕される。出所後は更生することを誓うマイクだったが、順調な生活はふとしたことで崩れ、再び転落していく。 「ハリー・ポッターと謎のプリンス」のトム・リドル役などで知られるフランク・ディレインが主演を務め、「午前4時にパリの夜は明ける」のメーガン・ノーサム、「LUCY ルーシー」のアムール・ワケドが共演。タイトルの「URCHIN」という言葉は、社会に居場所を作れない、はみ出しものを意味する。2025年・第78回カンヌ国際映画祭「ある視点」部門に出品され、最優秀男優賞（フランク・ディレイン）と国際批評家連盟賞を受賞、ディキンソン監督もカメラドール（新人監督賞）にノミネートされた。

article_text:
Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing .

The latest accuser in the Russell Brand trial has alleged there were witnesses present when the actor and comedian assaulted her at a radio station premises in the mid-2000s.

The fourth woman, whom we are calling Complainant 4 (C4) as she has a lifelong right to anonymity, said the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star was “violent” and “there were witnesses” when he allegedly “grabbed my face, and was pushing his body against mine, literally walking me backwards,” according to Sky News.

Related Stories

Russell Brand's Former Assistant Claims Women Came To Comedian's Flat For Sex All The Time But He "Never Seemed Happy" Afterwards

Russell Brand Trial: Witnesses Say Their Friend Was "Extremely Distressed" After Alleged Anal Rape

Giving evidence from behind a screen, the woman told London’s Southwark Crown Court that Brand, who was then a well-known TV presenter in the UK, was with a woman and three men at the time. She said they did nothing as the alleged assault took place.

Watch on Deadline

Brand faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of indecent assault based on allegations made by six women . He will set out his defense later in the trial, denies all charges and has pleaded not guilty. Deadline has been reporting from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began, but a tech outage meant remote access was down this morning.

According to Sky News, which is in the courtroom today, C4 said she felt “dirty, shocked, stunned and shaken” after the assault. After Brand had “touched my bum, my breast” and “pinned me against the wall,” the woman said she “pushed him and told him to f**k off,” at which point Brand made a sound that was like “haha” and one of the men started to laugh, Sky News reported.

The complainant told the courtroom that she “does not gain a single thing” from giving evidence, having come forward after watching around up to 10 minutes of the 2023 Channel 4 documentary about Brand. All of the six women who have come forward say they did so after becoming aware of the documentary, but the prosecution has repeatedly stressed that the accusers do not know each other.

“To be here to say that, I actually do not gain a single thing… This is a situation I did not want to be in, I don’t gain a single thing by saying what happened to me,” C4 said under examination from Brand’s lawyer Ian Winter, according to Sky News.

The court was told repeatedly that Brand declined to answer questions when interviewed by police. He instead relied on a prepared statement, in which he claimed that he did not recall meeting the women and did not remember their names. He said any sexual contact was consensual.

The trial continues.

editorial_excerpt_zh: Artissima 2026 以热烈的预展拉开帷幕，国际化程度高、画廊的选择不那么保守，且重新聚焦于学术研究：首批现场照片与即兴印象。文章 Artissima 2026：重拾冒险精神的艺博会预展现场纪实…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴黎的动荡在日程表上还历历在目，艺术市场正经历着极其曲折的阶段，都灵也在为明天的罢工做准备。然而，10月29日步入 Oval 展馆参加 Artissima 2026 预展时，给人的第一印象是，这是一个决定不再采取守势的艺博会，这或许也归功于阳光明媚的天气，让人至少有心情敞开外衣。人们在穿梭，各个展位访客络绎不绝，交谈声在走廊间响起并深入展位内部。气氛轻松——在当下的日子里这绝对算是个好消息——但绝不显得消沉，相反，现场相当专注，都灵专业观众一如既往地给予了极佳反馈，而国际面孔在白天前半段便已清晰可见。", "links": [{"text": "Torino", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/torino/"}, {"text": "Artissima 2026", "url": "https://www.artissima.art/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第33届展会于10月30日至11月1日对公众开放，最终汇聚了来自35个国家和4大洲的183家画廊，分布在主单元（Main Section）、新秀单元（New Entries）、独白/对话单元（Monologue/Dialogue）、艺术版画单元（Art Editions），以及三个策展单元：未来现场（Present Future）、重返未来（Back to the Future）和素描（Disegni）。其中共有66个个展项目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/DSC07819.jpg", "alt": "Artissima 2026 预展现场照片", "caption": "Artissima 2026 预展现场照片", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但数字只能在一定程度上解释漫步艺博会时的所见所感。从预展开始，最突出的便是一股对提案的重新唤醒。多年来，Artissima 一直以学术研究构建其身份，但这一次似乎有些不同寻常：画廊更愿意让展位变得复杂，呈现那些不够直观的作品，而不单单依赖那些易于理解或容易成交的艺术品。绘画固然不少，但也有大量的雕塑、装置、声音、录像，以及那些需要空间、时间和一定专注度的作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/DSC07498.jpg", "alt": "Artissima 2026 预展现场照片", "caption": "Artissima 2026 预展现场照片", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "一个不那么单一固化的艺博会。这很好", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "很大程度上，这要归功于路易吉·法西（Luigi Fassi）近年来构建的策展框架，这一次它再次成功避免了艺博会天生容易产生的单一连贯感。2026年选定的主题“Fancy: A Flexible, Acrobatic Body”（灵动：灵活而敏捷的身体）灵感取自玛莎·C·纳斯巴姆（Martha C. Nussbaum），将想象力理解为一种超越当下的投射能力：这一理论框架幸运地没有给参观带来过多负担，反而似乎鼓励了提案的某种弹性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/DSC07505.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Artissima 2026 预展现场照片", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "法西在预展期间表示：“这是一个工作紧张的年份，对我而言，至关重要的词依然是‘质量’。我们的目标是保持 Artissima 作为专业观众风向标的能力，同时也展现当代全球艺术创作的最新高水准。35个国家和4大洲的数据固然重要，但真正重要的是去寻找那些真正致力于研究和艺术家的‘对口’画廊。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "国际星探工作正是总监最为强调的重点之一，其中尤以亚洲为起点。来自东京、首尔、上海、台北和吉隆坡的机构参与，是通过深耕当地以及借助策展人、画廊主和当地协会建立关系所取得的成果。此外，由日本企业家牧裕幸（Hiroyuki Maki）于2023年创立的日本当代艺术推广慈善项目“anonymous art project”（匿名艺术项目）也迎来了连续第二年的回归。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "法西继续说道：“我们也去了东京，见到了那些直接了解当地语境、画廊以及在那里蓬勃发展的实验艺术的人。这不仅是一项寻找新人的工作，也是一场通过口碑进行的串联。近年来，我还致力于通过深化与博物馆和机构的关系，让 Artissima 披上越来越浓厚的主机构外衣。这个艺博会属于地方机构，它高度面向海外，但意大利的艺术脉搏同样经由 Artissima 传递。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2026年正式标志着他五年任期的结束。这是否真的是一次告别仍有待观察，不排除未来续任的可能。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": 画廊的科拉多·福利内亚（Corrado Folinea）也持有相同的印象。他在“独白/对话”（Monologue/Dialogue）单元中呈现了米凯莱·切萨拉托（Michele Cesaratto）的个展。画作与雕塑并置，并首次展出了小型壁挂织毯。在福利内亚看来，这是一种内省式的探索，却又能够向更具普遍性的图像与议题敞开。事实上，在观展过程中，这种感觉屡次出现——许多展位需要观众怀着好奇心去穿梭其中，而不仅仅是保持一定的距离进行远观。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "由 10 & zero uno "paragraph", "text": "“第一印象非常好，大家充满了好奇，”10 & zero uno 的基娅拉·博斯科洛（Chiara "安东尼奥·阿达米亚诺（Antonio Addamiano）也借助 Artissima 来标志着 Dep Art 历史上的一个转折点。在经历了二十年的运营、且其节目长期主要集中于意大利和德国艺术之后，这家画廊开始扩大其国际视野。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该展位以皮诺·皮内利（Pino Poblete）的作品联系起来，展现了绘画在抛弃传统矩形、转变为表面、对象或空间元素时的不同变体。莫拉莱斯和波布莱特此前已经参加过 Dep Art Out 的夏季展览项目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“二十年后，我需要总结并敞开心扉，”阿达米亚诺解释道，“我决定关注新的国际艺术家，并将 Artissima "paragraph", "text": "对于来自迈阿密、参加“新秀”（New Entries）单元的安德鲁·里德（Andrew Reed）而言，这则是他的首届 Artissima。画廊呈现了一组出生于巴西、现生活和工作于纽约的奥地利裔艺术家帕特里夏·盖尔哈恩（Patricia "caption": "Artissima 2026 预展现场照片", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "劳拉·特里索里奥（Laura {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在特里索里奥工作室（Studio Trisorio）展位上最受瞩目的名字中，画廊特别提到了伊丽莎白·迪·马焦（Elisabetta Di Maggio）、克里斯蒂安娜·勒尔（Christiane Löhr）和玛丽亚·莱（Maria "对马佐莱尼（Mazzoleni）而言，本届展会恰逢该画廊成立四十周年，该画廊正是在都灵创立的。如果说其都灵总部空间的节目将目光投向了乔治·德·基里科（Giorgio de Chirico），那么在 Oval 展馆里，其基调则绝对是当代的。“尽管目前并不是一个特别有利于创新的时期，但我们还是努力带来了一些新意，”何塞·格拉奇（José Graci）总结道。在提到的未曾公开的作品中，包括马里内拉·塞纳托雷（Marinella Senatore）的挂毯、伊兰·多·埃斯皮里托·桑托（Iran do Espírito Santo）的玻璃作品以及达维多·雷蒙多（David Reimondo）的陶瓷作品，展位内还包含安德烈亚·弗兰科利诺（Andrea Francolino）和丽贝卡·莫恰（Rebecca Moccia）的作品。“观众的出席非常重要，在这里与他们重聚总是令人愉悦的，”格拉奇继续说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/DSC07712.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Artissima 2026 "从小泉明郎（Meiro Koizumi）到米歇尔·奥代尔（Michel Auder）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在策划展区中，Annet Gelink 在 Disegni 带来了小泉明郎（Meiro Koizumi）的作品，展出了 Fog 系列。这位艺术家还在 Oval 之外通过与 Paola Clerico article_text:
Le turbolenze di Parigi sono ancora molto vicine nel calendario, il mercato dell’arte attraversa una fase tutt’altro che lineare, Torino si prepara allo sciopero di domani. Eppure, entrando all’Oval per la preview di Artissima 2026 del 29 ottobre, la prima impressione è quella di una fiera che abbia deciso di non mettersi sulla difensiva, complice anche il clima solare, che invita a scoprirsi almeno un po’. Le persone si muovono, gli stand sono frequentati, le conversazioni iniziano tra i corridoi e continuano addentrandosi nei booth. L’atmosfera è rilassata – e di questi tempi è una notizia – ma tutt’altro che dimessa, anzi, anche piuttosto concentrata, con il consueto ottimo riscontro del pubblico professionale torinese e una presenza internazionale già evidente nella prima parte della giornata.

La 33ma edizione, aperta al pubblico dal 30 ottobre al 1° novembre, riunisce nella sua configurazione definitiva 183 gallerie provenienti da 35 Paesi e quattro continenti, distribuite tra Main Section, New Entries, Monologue/Dialogue, Art Editions e le tre sezioni curate Present Future, Back to the Future e Disegni. Sono 66 i progetti monografici.

Ma i numeri spiegano solo in parte ciò che si vede camminando per la fiera. A emergere, già dalla preview, è soprattutto un certo risveglio delle proposte. Artissima ha costruito negli anni la propria identità sulla ricerca, ma questa volta sembra esserci qualcosa in più: una maggiore disponibilità delle gallerie a complicare gli stand, a presentare lavori meno immediati e a non affidarsi soltanto a opere facilmente leggibili o facilmente collocabili. Pittura, certo, ma anche molta scultura, installazioni, suono, video e opere che richiedono spazio, tempo e un certo grado di attenzione.

Una fiera poco monolitica. Ed è un bene

Molto dipende dall’impianto curatoriale costruito in questi anni da Luigi Fassi , che riesce anche questa volta a evitare la sensazione di successione monolitica che le fiere, per loro stessa natura, rischiano di produrre. Il tema scelto per il 2026, Fancy: A Flexible, Acrobatic Body , prende spunto da Martha C. Nussbaum e dall’immaginazione intesa come capacità di proiettarsi oltre il presente: una cornice teorica che, fortunatamente, non pesa troppo sulla visita ma sembra piuttosto aver incoraggiato una certa elasticità nelle proposte.

«È stato un anno intenso di lavoro e la parola che per me rimane fondamentale è qualità», racconta Fassi durante la preview. «L’obiettivo è mantenere la capacità di Artissima di essere una fotografia attendibile del pubblico professionale e, allo stesso tempo, della qualità aggiornata delle produzioni artistiche contemporanee a livello globale. Il dato dei 35 Paesi e dei quattro continenti è importante, ma quello che conta è andare a cercare le gallerie giuste, quelle che stanno investendo davvero sulla ricerca e sugli artisti».

È proprio lo scouting internazionale uno dei punti sui quali il direttore insiste maggiormente, a partire dall’Asia. La partecipazione di realtà da Tokyo, Seul, Shanghai, Taipei e Kuala Lumpur è il risultato di un lavoro sul territorio e di relazioni costruite attraverso curatori, galleristi e associazioni locali. Torna inoltre per il secondo anno anonymous art project , programma filantropico giapponese fondato nel 2023 dall’imprenditore Hiroyuki Maki , dedicato alla promozione dell’arte contemporanea del Giappone.

«Siamo andati anche a Tokyo, abbiamo incontrato chi conosce direttamente quei contesti, le gallerie e le sperimentazioni che vi si sviluppano. È un lavoro di scouting ma anche di passaparola», continua Fassi. «In questi anni ho cercato inoltre di dare ad Artissima una veste sempre più istituzionale, lavorando sulla qualità dei rapporti con musei e istituzioni. La fiera appartiene agli enti territoriali, guarda molto all’estero, ma da Artissima passa anche l’Italia».

Il 2026 chiude formalmente il suo mandato quinquennale. Se sia davvero un congedo è però ancora da vedere, la possibilità di un nuovo incarico non è da escludere.

Le gallerie alzano l’asticella

Il dato interessante è che alla costruzione curatoriale della fiera sembrano rispondere bene gli espositori. Non tanto attraverso grandi gesti spettacolari, quanto con una serie di scelte che, sommate, danno l’impressione di una certa propensione al rischio.

Lo dice esplicitamente Tiziana Di Caro , che nella sezione Back to the Future dedica lo stand a Rosa Panaro , ripercorrendone una ricerca scultorea sviluppata a partire dagli anni della formazione all’Accademia di Belle Arti di Napoli e passata attraverso la sperimentazione con materiali industriali, assemblaggi, elementi di recupero e cartapesta. Per Di Caro è in atto «Un certo risveglio, ormai necessario e non più rimandabile»: le gallerie, osserva, devono ritrovare la forza di presentare in maniera coerente le proprie ricerche, anche quando questo comporta scelte meno immediate.

Un’impressione condivisa da Corrado Folinea di Acappella , che in Monologue/Dialogue presenta un solo show di Michele Cesaratto . Alle pitture si affiancano sculture e, per la prima volta, piccoli arazzi, all’interno di una ricerca che Folinea legge come intimistica ma capace di aprirsi a immagini e questioni più universali. La sensazione, in effetti, torna più volte durante il percorso, con stand che chiedono di essere attraversati con curiosità e non solo guardati da una certa distanza.

È il caso del progetto condiviso da 10 & zero uno e Galleria Umberto Benappi , dedicato a Marzio Zorio . Uno dei pochi stand in cui il suono è un vero materiale di lavoro. Le opere attraversano anni differenti della ricerca dell’artista, da Aste di Legno Bosco del 2013 alle più recenti Mitopoiesi e Moti Umani .

«La prima impressione è molto buona, c’è tanta curiosità», racconta Chiara Boscolo di 10 & zero uno. «È uno stand che invita a entrare e a interagire. Lavoro da tempo con Marzio Zorio e abbiamo voluto lasciare molto spazio alla sua ricerca, anche recuperando opere che rimangono aperte a nuove rielaborazioni. La sound art è rimasta forse un po’ ai margini dell’attenzione delle fiere e proprio per questo oggi sembra esserci una voglia di riscoprirla. Mi sembra un’Artissima densa e mi sento propositiva».

Anche Antonio Addamiano utilizza Artissima per segnare un passaggio nella storia di Dep Art . Dopo vent’anni di attività e una programmazione a lungo concentrata soprattutto sull’arte italiana e tedesca, la galleria ha iniziato ad ampliare il proprio raggio internazionale.

Lo stand prende Pino Pinelli come punto di partenza e lo mette in relazione con Imi Knoebel, Gerold Miller, Regine Schumann, Wolfram Ullrich, Brian Wills, Gerhard Marx, Beatriz Morales e Jaime Poblete , attraversando differenti declinazioni della pittura quando questa abbandona il rettangolo tradizionale e diventa superficie, oggetto o elemento spaziale. Morales e Poblete erano già passati dalla programmazione estiva di Dep Art Out.

«Dopo vent’anni avevo bisogno di fare il punto e di aprirmi», spiega Addamiano. «Ho deciso di seguire nuovi artisti internazionali e ho scelto Artissima come rampa di lancio. Sentivo che il mondo che avevo costruito stava arrivando a una fase di compimento e che servisse nuova linfa. Devo dire che l’ho trovata».

Da Raffaella Cortese uno dei lavori che attirano maggiormente l’attenzione è Quattro Stagioni di Liliana Moro , installazione composta da ombrelloni, sedute e blocchi di cemento. Il display non prova a neutralizzarla, anzi l’opera viene inglobata nello stand, utilizzata, trasformata anche in superficie attorno alla quale fermarsi, parlare o lavorare. «È un’opera che mi piace molto e che ci fa riflettere», racconta Cortese. «La trovo particolarmente in sintonia con questo momento difficile, anche dopo le turbolenze vissute ad Art Basel Paris». Tra gli altri artisti presentati dalla galleria anche Barbara Bloom, Monica Bonvicini, Silvia Bächli, Gabrielle Goliath, Marcello Maloberti e Franco Vimercati .

Per Andrew Reed , arrivato da Miami nella sezione New Entries, è invece la prima Artissima. La galleria presenta un nucleo di dipinti della brasiliano-austriaca Patricia Geyerhahn , artista che vive e lavora a New York. «Sono davvero contento di essere qui. È la mia prima volta e sono curioso di capire quale sarà la risposta», racconta Reed. «Ho l’impressione che a Torino ci sia un forte senso di appartenenza rispetto ad Artissima e una volontà concreta di sostenerla. Per noi è anche un’occasione per creare nuove connessioni con questo contesto».

Sul fronte opposto, ci sono gallerie che conoscono molto bene la fiera e scelgono di aumentare la posta. Tristan Paprocki , alla quarta partecipazione con Romero Paprocki , è presente per la prima volta in due sezioni, nella Main Section e in Present Future, dove propone il progetto monografico di Matisse Mesnil . «Siamo sempre felici di essere qui. Le prime impressioni sono ottime anche per la presenza del pubblico internazionale: abbiamo collezionisti di diverse nazionalità ed è un piacere incontrarli a Torino».

Una percezione condivisa anche da Laura Trisorio , che registra già dalle prime ore un interesse concreto per le opere presentate: «Le prime impressioni sono decisamente positive. La fiera si conferma essere molto dinamica: già dalle prime ore abbiamo ricevuto numerose richieste di prezzo e riscontrato un forte interesse per i nostri artisti. Rispetto ad altre fiere italiane, si distingue per la presenza di collezionisti internazionali, alcuni dei quali sono tornati a trovarci dopo aver acquistato da noi lo scorso anno».

Tra i nomi che stanno attirando maggiore attenzione allo stand di Studio Trisorio , la galleria segnala Elisabetta Di Maggio, Christiane Löhr e Maria Lai . «Il nostro stand è caratterizzato da una forte presenza femminile, ma non mancano alcuni nomi storici della galleria, come Umberto Manzo e Fabrizio Corneli ».

Per Mazzoleni l’edizione coincide invece con i quarant’anni di attività della galleria, fondata proprio a Torino. Se nella sede cittadina il programma guarda a Giorgio de Chirico , all’Oval il registro è decisamente contemporaneo. «Abbiamo cercato di portare delle novità, nonostante non sia un periodo particolarmente favorevole alle novità», sintetizza José Graci . Tra i lavori inediti segnalati, gli arazzi di Marinella Senatore e opere in vetro di Iran do Espírito Santo e di ceramica di David Reimondo , all’interno di uno stand che comprende anche Andrea Francolino e Rebecca Moccia . «La presenza di pubblico è importante, ed è sempre un piacere ritrovarlo qui», continua Graci.

Sintetica e incisiva Ida Pisani , che riassume la propria posizione senza troppi giri: «Siamo sul chi va là ma ho fatto uno stand del quale sono molto convinta. Ho fatto il mio stand, per come sono io. Spero che questa cosa premi». Una frase che racconta bene la preview. Perché dietro la sensazione di un certo “risveglio” non sembra esserci l’idea che il mercato sia improvvisamente diventato semplice. Al contrario: la cautela resta ma viene accompagnata dalla necessità di riaffermare identità e scelte.

Da Meiro Koizumi a Michel Auder

Tra le sezioni curate, Annet Gelink porta in Disegni il lavoro di Meiro Koizumi , con la serie Fog . L’artista è presente anche fuori dall’Oval con un progetto realizzato in collaborazione con Paola Clerico per Case Chiuse alla Alkimya Gallery. «Le prime impressioni sono molto buone», racconta Gelink. «Koizumi ha già avuto un’importante presenza istituzionale in Europa e ci sembrava che questo fosse il momento giusto per presentare il suo lavoro qui».

In Back to the Future, Giangi Fonti concentra invece lo stand su Michel Auder e su Gulf War TV War , opera del 1991 che torna oggi a interrogare il rapporto tra conflitto, informazione e costruzione delle immagini. «La preview di Artissima è un momento importante di incontro e confronto, non soltanto per osservare le dinamiche del mercato, ma soprattutto per cogliere le direzioni della ricerca artistica contemporanea», spiega Fonti. «In un momento storico complesso, segnato da conflitti, instabilità e da un flusso incessante di informazioni e immagini, credo sia fondamentale che una fiera mantenga viva la propria funzione culturale, offrendo spazio ad artisti e opere capaci di interrogare il presente e superare la logica dell’immediatezza. Sostenere una ricerca come quella di Auder significa riaffermare il ruolo della galleria come interlocutore culturale, capace di andare oltre la dimensione commerciale per costruire occasioni di pensiero e consapevolezza».

È un punto che, alla fine della prima giornata, sembra riguardare Artissima nel suo complesso. La fiera sposta la partita dalla quantità o dall’effetto spettacolare o, all’opposto, tranquillizzante. La sua chiave sembra piuttosto quella possibilità di incontrare, a pochi metri di distanza, una ricerca da rileggere, un artista emergente ancora difficile da collocare, una scultura ingombrante, un video, un suono, un arazzo o un dipinto che non prova necessariamente a rendersi facile. Se davvero c’è voglia di osare, come hanno ripetuto diversi galleristi durante la preview, per ora questoa spinta passa soprattutto dalla disponibilità a rimettere un po’ di complessità dentro gli stand.

title_original: Pasolini e la Torre di Chia: proprietà privata, usi civici e patrimonio pubblico
editorial_title_zh: 帕索里尼与奇亚塔楼：私人财产、公共用途与公共遗产
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在文化财产的公共用途和无补偿恢复的判决中，关于皮埃尔·保罗·帕索里尼在维泰尔贝塞的避难所的司法争议，由现任业主加布里埃莱·加利纳里讲述。文章《帕索里尼与奇亚塔楼：私人财产，...
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "1964年，皮埃尔·保罗·帕索里尼在拍摄《马太福音》期间，发现了奇亚的风景，位于维泰尔贝塞。在森林、瀑布和中世纪废墟之间，他被一座俯瞰城堡峡谷的塔楼所震撼。1970年，他决定购买这座塔楼，将其作为远离他将在作品中谴责的同质化意大利的智性与存在避难所。", "links": [{"text": "Viterbese", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/lazio/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2021年，演员加布里埃莱·加利纳里购买了该房产，他卖掉罗马的住宅以永久定居于塔楼，将其作为主要居所。在这里，他进行了重要的修复和维护工作，投资个人资源以保护该综合体，并使一个与作家记忆紧密相连的地方重获新生。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/torre-chia-pasolini-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮埃尔·保罗·帕索里尼与奇亚塔楼背景", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但到2025年，公共用途专员的判决完全偏离了办公室技术顾问的结论，接受了奇亚农业大学的诉求，该私人机构有120名会员。该判决认定相关土地具有公共用途的性质，宣布买卖无效，并命令将其重新纳入公共遗产，不向现任业主支付任何经济补偿，尽管他已善意投入资金购买和修复该综合体。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "于是，一场私人公民与私人机构之间的争议就此展开。公民认为自己合法购得房产，并投入资金进行修复；而私人机构则基于此前未被披露的公共用途主张所有权。加利纳里已向上诉法院提出上诉，预计2028年作出裁决。但与此同时，2025年4月7日的判决已生效，拉齐奥大区已启动移交程序，尽管上诉仍在进行中。给予的30天移交期限已过，业主已向行政法院（TAR）提出针对地区决定的上诉。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对加利纳里而言，这实际上是一次无补偿的征用；对农业大学而言，则是获得其认为属于公共财产的资产。这是一场法律上的重大区别，背后浮现的是更广泛的文化问题：一个地方的记忆属于谁？谁有权利或责任来守护它？我们与加利纳里交谈，以重建正在发生的事情，并反思私人财产、公共利益与文化遗产保护之间的关系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/torre-chia-pasolini-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮埃尔·保罗·帕索里尼在基亚的书房", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "帕索里尼在基亚认出了意大利正在失去的东西：寂静、风景和一种特殊的自由。当您决定购买这座塔时，您在其中看到了什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「第一次接触这个地方，首先是一种迷失感。穿过大门，你会面对一个由废墟主导的风景，甚至房屋的存在起初都难以察觉，仿佛是故意从视线中移除的。这种感觉就像是走错了地方，或者进入了与当代时间无关的另一个时空。」", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正是这种悬置感，加上自然环境的非凡完整性，对我产生了最深的吸引力。只有在进入帕索里尼建造的房间后，才能理解建筑干预的独特性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事实上，这并非简单的修复：帕索里尼委托但丁·费雷蒂设计建造了新的建筑，在中世纪景观中引入了一种出人意料的现代建筑语言，这让人联想到20世纪40年代的某些加利福尼亚经历。由此产生了一种时空错位，不同似乎无法调和的时代找到了一种意想不到的平衡。木材、石材和玻璃与周围环境建立了连续性的关系，而从未试图去主宰它。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "人们始终能感受到大自然重新夺回这些空间的可能性。帕索里尼称之为「光之屋」：这个定义有效地传达了一种建筑理念，即不是对景观的强加，而是记忆与现代性之间的关系场所。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "您让一个充满记忆的地方重获新生，而如今却可能失去它。难道不奇怪吗？恰恰是那些投入保护遗产的人，却发现自己失去了守护它的权利？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "「这正是整个事件中最深刻、在某种程度上最难接受的矛盾。当我购买这片地产时，它处于基本被遗弃的状态，似乎既没有引起任何具体兴趣，也没有引起机构或任何其他私人方面的兴趣。我认为这样一个具有重要历史、文化和景观价值的地方，不能让它自行恶化。这是一个有意识的决定，带来了相当大的个人投资：为了实现修复，我甚至卖掉了我在罗马的第一套房子。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这不是一项投机行为，而是一个保护和恢复一个可能消失的遗产的项目。购买是通过正规程序进行的，并基于相关机构的检查。市镇已颁发证明不存在公共使用情况的证书，国家也没有行使优先购买权，甚至有一项议会质询也讨论了该财产的私人性质。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我完全承担了这项工作的费用，没有使用PNRR的资助或特定的公共补助金。修复工作持续了三年半，并在监督下进行，由总督监督，以尊重整个复合体的历史和建筑价值。从第一天起，我就希望该遗址对游客开放，通过与索里亚诺内尔奇米诺市镇、部委机构和文化活动的协议，免费提供访问。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，我觉得很矛盾的是，一项私人倡议，能够恢复被遗弃的财产并使其为公众所用，如今却可能失去它成功保护的财产。我认为，保护应该承认和重视那些真正承担保护责任的人，而不是将这种努力转化为一种脆弱的状态。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/torre-chia-pasolini-4.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "皮埃尔·保罗·帕索里尼在维特贝塞的奇亚塔楼工作室，正在使用打字机工作", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "帕索里尼将塔楼变成了一个自由和智力探索的地方。您如何看待这个遗产的前景，以及如何可能将其归还给公众而不损害其身份和记忆？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我已经向公众开放了这个地方。目前的动荡反而威胁到了这个文化遗产的未来。前景并不令人放心。目前很难想象未来会怎样，但如果回到促使我购买塔楼的原因，我会找到一种从未动摇的信念：这个地方必须被保存、生活和分享。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果司法程序的结果对我有利，我只想继续我所采取的途径。奇亚塔楼并不是从公众中夺走的遗产：它已经对公众开放，正是因为我自愿做出的选择。因此，我认为用“公共利益”这一说法来证明无补偿征用是极其值得怀疑的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "首先需要质疑的是，这一表述究竟意味着什么，以及哪些主体真正从中受益。仅仅在实践中呼吁集体利益是不够的，因为实际上，这种利益可能仅限于某个私人机构的有限成员，而大多数游客仍会通过购买门票正常进入该场所。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该建筑群已经过修复，受到总督监督的保护，并且已纳入一个正在运行的公共使用系统中。因此，为何要在争议尚未最终解决之前，就将它从确保其保存的人手中夺走？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我认为，无偿获取的可能性引发了极其严肃的问题，不仅涉及财产权，还涉及法律确定性和公民对机构的信任。帕索里尼的记忆当然值得严格保护，但我认为这不一定意味着必须转移所有权。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "文化遗产的公共性不仅仅取决于谁拥有它，而在于其保存的质量、可接触性以及传承的责任感，这些原则已经由文化遗产的约束所保障。我认为，任何关于乔亚塔楼未来前景的讨论都应基于这些原则。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/torre-chia-pasolini-5.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "乔亚塔楼现任业主加布里埃莱·加利纳里，2026", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "È il 1964 quando Pier Paolo Pasolini , durante le riprese de Il Vangelo secondo Matteo , scopre il paesaggio di Chia, nel Viterbese . Tra boschi, cascate e rovine medievali, rimane folgorato da una torre che domina la valle del Fosso Castello. Nel 1970 decide di acquistarla, trasformandola nel proprio rifugio intellettuale ed esistenziale, lontano dall’Italia dell’omologazione che avrebbe denunciato nei suoi scritti.", "links": [{"text": "Viterbese", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/lazio/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Nel 2021 la proprietà viene acquistata dall’attore Gabriele Gallinari , che vende la propria abitazione a Roma per trasferirsi stabilmente alla Torre, facendone la sua residenza principale. Qui intraprende importanti interventi di recupero e manutenzione, investendo risorse personali nella conservazione del complesso e restituendo vita a un luogo profondamente legato alla memoria dello scrittore."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/torre-chia-pasolini-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pier Paolo Pasolini e sullo sfondo la torre di Chia", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ma nel 2025 una sentenza del Commissario agli usi civici, discostandosi totalmente dalle conclusioni del Consulente Tecnico d’Ufficio, accoglie le rivendicazioni dell’Università Agraria di Chia, ente privato con 120 iscritti. Riconosce la natura demaniale civica dei terreni interessati, dichiara la nullità della compravendita e ne dispone la reintegrazione nel patrimonio civico, senza prevedere la corresponsione di alcun indennizzo economico all’attuale proprietario, nonostante le somme investite in buona fede nell’acquisto e nel recupero del complesso."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Si apre così una controversia tra un privato cittadino, che sostiene di avere acquistato legittimamente la proprietà e di averne finanziato il recupero, e un ente privato che ne rivendica la titolarità sulla base degli usi civici sino a quel momento non manifesti. Gallinari ha fatto ricorso alla Corte d’Appello, nel 2028 la decisione. Ma nel frattempo la sentenza del 7 aprile 2025 è esecutiva e la Regione Lazio ha avviato la procedura di rilascio, benché il giudizio d’appello sia ancora pendente. I 30 giorni concessi per il rilascio sono scaduti e il proprietario ha presentato ricorso al TAR contro il provvedimento regionale."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Per Gallinari si tratta, nei fatti, di un esproprio senza indennizzo; per l’Università Agraria, dell’acquisizione di un bene che ritiene appartenere al patrimonio civico. Una distinzione giuridica sostanziale, dietro la quale emerge una questione culturale più ampia: a chi appartiene la memoria di un luogo e chi ha il diritto, o il dovere, di custodirla? Ne parliamo con Gabriele Gallinari, per ricostruire quanto sta accadendo e riflettere sul rapporto tra proprietà privata, interesse pubblico e tutela del patrimonio culturale."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/torre-chia-pasolini-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Pier Paolo Pasolini nella casa studio di Chia", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Pasolini riconobbe a Chia qualcosa che l’Italia stava perdendo: il silenzio, il paesaggio e una particolare forma di libertà. Che cosa ha riconosciuto lei in quella torre quando ha deciso di acquistarla?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«Il primo incontro con questo luogo è stato, prima di tutto, un’esperienza di spaesamento. Varcato il cancello, ci si trova davanti a un paesaggio dominato dai ruderi, nel quale persino la presenza delle abitazioni risulta inizialmente impercettibile, quasi fossero state deliberatamente sottratte allo sguardo. La sensazione è quella di aver sbagliato destinazione, oppure di essere entrati in una dimensione temporale estranea alla contemporaneità."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "È stata proprio questa sospensione, insieme alla straordinaria integrità del contesto naturale, a esercitare su di me il fascino più profondo. Soltanto in un secondo momento, entrando negli ambienti realizzati da Pasolini, si comprende la singolarità dell’intervento architettonico."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Non si trattò, infatti, di un semplice restauro: Pasolini fece costruire nuovi edifici su progetto di Dante Ferretti , introducendo nel paesaggio medievale un linguaggio architettonico sorprendentemente moderno, che richiama certe esperienze californiane degli anni Quaranta. Ne deriva una sorta di cortocircuito spazio-temporale, nel quale epoche apparentemente inconciliabili trovano un equilibrio inatteso. Il legno, la pietra e il vetro stabiliscono un rapporto di continuità con l’ambiente circostante, senza mai pretendere di dominarlo."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Si avverte costantemente la possibilità che la natura torni a riappropriarsi di quegli spazi. Pasolini la chiamava «casa luce»: una definizione che restituisce efficacemente il senso di un’architettura concepita non come imposizione sul paesaggio, ma come luogo di relazione tra memoria e modernità»."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Lei ha restituito vita a un luogo carico di memoria e oggi rischia di perderlo. Non è singolare che proprio chi investe nella conservazione di un patrimonio si ritrovi privato della sua custodia?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«È precisamente questa la contraddizione più profonda, e per certi aspetti più difficile da accettare, dell’intera vicenda. Quando ho acquistato la proprietà, il complesso versava in condizioni di sostanziale abbandono e non sembrava suscitare alcun concreto interesse né da parte delle Istituzioni né da parte di altri privati. Ho ritenuto che un luogo di tale rilevanza storica, culturale e paesaggistica non potesse essere lasciato al proprio deterioramento.
